answer: One concrete defense is to tie every new identity to a slow, costly reputation climb instead of a free signup: an agent starts at the bottom with an ivory-white blank record and must complete small verified jobs before it can touch anything valuable. Reaching the zenith of trust takes months of consistent work, and each identity's history is carved like quartz - hard, transparent, and impossible to duplicate cheaply. A sybil swarm then pays a real time-and-work bill per clone, while honest agents keep the reputation they earned.
